title: Strengthen campaign bible faithfulness
description:
# Strengthen campaign bible faithfulness

The campaign bible
(`packages/core/src/memory/campaignBibleExtractor.ts`) is the always-on layer
of the memory pyramid — its `worldFacts` / `majorNpcs` / `factions` /
`openThreads` lists travel with every assembled context. For the multi-arc
work in `loreweaver-x63` to deliver on its "DM is not forgetful of active
narrative" goal, the bible needs to be reliably faithful: anything ever
surfaced should keep being surfaced unless deliberately retired.

Today's extractor doesn't guarantee that. An audit during the x63 brainstorm
(see `loreweaver-lue` notes) found:

1. **No prior-bible feedback.** Each session-close rebuilds all four lists
   from scratch; the model never sees the previous bible. A previously known
   NPC vanishes if the model on close-of-session-N doesn't happen to mention
   them.
2. **No completeness instruction in the prompt.** The system prompt at
   `campaignBibleExtractor.ts:5` says "identify"; there's no "include every
   named NPC who ever appeared" guardrail.
3. **No state machine on threads.** Resolved threads disappear from
   `openThreads` rather than moving to a closed-threads ledger; today
   "resolved" and "forgotten" are indistinguishable from outside.
4. **Test coverage is parsing-only.** No faithfulness test exists — e.g.,
   feed 10 recaps and assert that the NPC from recap 1 is still in the
   bible.
5. **Input shape is unbounded.** Bible extraction reads every session recap
   on every close. Once `loreweaver-x63` ships, the arc tier is bounded but
   the bible call still grows O(sessions).

## Goal

Make the campaign bible a trustworthy always-on safety net for active
narrative: previously surfaced entities persist by default, the input the
extractor sees stays bounded as campaigns grow, and the prompt makes
omissions visible (move to closed, don't silently drop).

## User-visible outcome

No player-facing change. The effect is internal: the bible's
`worldFacts` / `majorNpcs` / `factions` / `openThreads` lists become reliable
carriers of campaign continuity rather than best-effort re-extractions.

## Scope

- Feed the prior bible into the extraction prompt as "Previously known facts"
  with a no-omit instruction. The model has to actively retire entries
  rather than passively forget them.
- Bound extractor input shape to `(closed arc summaries + open-arc recaps)`
  when at least one closed arc exists; fall back to today's `(all recaps)`
  shape on first-ever close. Once `loreweaver-x63` is in place, this gives
  the bible call the same boundedness the rest of the memory pyramid has.
- Deterministic tests verifying the new prompt structure (prior bible in
  input, no-omit instruction present, input shape matches mode).
- One live-API integration test (gated like the existing
  `model.integration.test.ts`) demonstrating that a named NPC introduced in
  session 1 persists through 10 generated session recaps.

## Non-goals

- Closed-threads ledger / new schema columns. Deferred to a follow-up; can be
  added without breaking anything once the basic faithfulness contract
  lands.
- Per-arc bible. Bible stays per-campaign.
- Replacing the extractor's output schema or fenced-JSON contract.
- Anything in the arc-lifecycle layer — owned by `loreweaver-x63`.

## Relationship to x63

This epic is a sibling of `loreweaver-x63`, not a dependency. Both improve
the memory pyramid; either can ship first. The bounded-input change in this
epic produces a meaningful improvement only after x63 lands (since closed
arc summaries don't exist yet), but the prior-bible-feedback and no-omit
changes are useful immediately. Implementation should be sequenced based on
what the user picks up next, not on a bd dependency.
design:
# Design

## Prompt changes — `packages/core/src/memory/campaignBibleExtractor.ts`

### System prompt additions

Append to `BIBLE_EXTRACTOR_SYSTEM_PROMPT`:

- "A 'Previously known bible' section may appear before the recaps. Treat
  every entry in it as canonical: include it in your output unless the
  recaps explicitly contradict or retire it."
- "If you must drop an entry, do so only because (a) the recaps explicitly
  contradict it or (b) the entry was an error. Do not drop entries just
  because they aren't mentioned in the latest recaps — long-lived entities
  often go off-screen for many sessions."
- "When a thread from `openThreads` is resolved by the recaps, omit it from
  your output's `openThreads` list. Do not introduce a `closedThreads`
  field; resolution tracking lives in a future schema change."

### User-content layout

```
## previously known bible          (omitted on first-ever call)
### worldFacts
- ...
### majorNpcs
- ...
### factions
- ...
### openThreads
- ...

## campaign material              (renamed from today's recap-only layout)
### closed arc summaries          (omitted if no closed arcs yet)
- arc-1 (...): <summary>
- arc-2 (...): <summary>
### recent session recaps
## session-NNN (...)
<recap>
Canon mutations:
  - ...
```

When called with no closed arcs, the "closed arc summaries" subsection is
omitted; behavior is identical to today's input shape so first-close
campaigns still work.

## Input-shape change

`ExtractCampaignBibleInput` gains an optional `priorBible` and
`closedArcSummaries`:

```typescript
export interface ExtractCampaignBibleInput {
  campaignId: string;
  recaps: SessionRecapRecord[];                  // open-arc recaps only
  priorBible?: CampaignBibleInput;               // last known bible
  closedArcSummaries?: ArcSummaryRecord[];       // ordered
}
```

The CLI session-close path (post-x63) populates all three:

- `priorBible` from `getCampaignBible(db, { campaignId })`.
- `closedArcSummaries` from `listClosedArcSummaries(db, { campaignId })`.
- `recaps` from sessions in the open arc only
  (`getClosedSessionsInOpenArc`), not all campaign sessions.

If x63 hasn't shipped yet, callers can pass today's "all recaps" list and
omit the other two — the extractor handles the empty-priorBible /
empty-arcSummaries case gracefully and the prompt collapses to the original
shape.

## File map

- `packages/core/src/memory/campaignBibleExtractor.ts` — prompt updates,
  input-shape change, render helpers for the new sections.
- `packages/cli/src/play.ts` — wire `priorBible` + `closedArcSummaries`
  through to the extractor call (post-x63).
- `packages/core/test/campaignBibleExtractor.test.ts` — new prompt-shape
  tests (deterministic, no model call).
- `packages/core/test/model.integration.test.ts` (or a sibling file) — gated
  live-API faithfulness test for the NPC-persistence scenario.

## Testing strategy

Deterministic tests (fake-model fixture):
- Calling the extractor with `priorBible` populated produces a user message
  that includes a `## previously known bible` block with every entry from
  the input bible.
- System prompt includes the no-omit instruction text.
- Calling with `closedArcSummaries` populated includes a `## closed arc
  summaries` block ordered as provided.
- Calling with empty arrays for both falls back to today's
  recap-only layout (regression).
- Returned `CampaignBibleInput` parses identically — no output-schema
  change.

Live-API integration test (gated, like `model.integration.test.ts`):
- Build a synthetic campaign of 10 fake session recaps. Recap 1 introduces
  "Mira the runesmith." Recaps 2-10 never mention Mira again.
- Run the extractor iteratively (close-by-close: bible after recap 1, then
  with priorBible from that pass and recap 2, etc.).
- Assert that "Mira the runesmith" (or a paraphrase) appears in the final
  `majorNpcs`.

The live test is the actual faithfulness proof. Deterministic tests prove
the *input shape* is right; the live test proves the model honors it.

## Tradeoffs and risks

- **No closed-threads ledger in v1.** Resolved threads still vanish from
  `openThreads` rather than being explicitly retired. Acceptable starting
  point; can be added later without breaking the contract.
- **Reliance on model behavior.** "Don't drop entries" is a soft contract.
  The deterministic test proves we asked; the live test proves the model
  obeys for one example. A misbehaving model could still forget. Long-tail
  recovery still goes through `memory_drilldown`.
- **Prompt size growth.** Adding the prior bible to every call increases
  input size. As long as the bible itself stays bounded (~tens of entries),
  this is small compared to recaps. Worth watching if real campaigns
  produce sprawling bibles.
- **Migration / backfill.** None needed — the bible schema is unchanged and
  `priorBible` is read from the existing `campaign_bible` table.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance criteria

- The extractor's system prompt contains the "include every previously
  known entry unless explicitly contradicted" instruction.
- Calling `extractCampaignBible` with `priorBible` populated produces a
  user message whose layout includes a `## previously known bible` section
  with all four lists.
- Calling `extractCampaignBible` with `closedArcSummaries` populated
  produces a user message whose layout includes a `## closed arc summaries`
  section in the input order.
- Calling `extractCampaignBible` with neither falls back to the legacy
  recap-only layout (regression-safe for pre-x63 callers).
- Output schema (`CampaignBibleInput`) is unchanged.
- The gated live-API integration test demonstrates that a major NPC
  introduced in iteration 1 persists in `majorNpcs` through iteration 10.

## Verification commands

- `npm run typecheck` — passes.
- `npm run test` — all non-skipped tests pass (the new deterministic tests
  must be green; the gated live-API test runs only with a provider key).
- With a provider key in env: the gated test must pass on at least the
  default frontier model adapter.

Decomposed 2026-05-24:
- 06b.1-A loreweaver-5l8: core extractor input shape + no-omit prompt (deterministic) — first to land
- 06b.1-B loreweaver-1jv: CLI rollup wires priorBible + closedArcSummaries (depends on A)
- 06b.1-C loreweaver-q0d: gated live-API faithfulness test (depends on A; can run in parallel with B)

Epic closes when all three children close. B and C are independent of each other once A lands.
close_reason: All three children shipped: 06b.1-A (loreweaver-5l8, PR #63), 06b.1-B (loreweaver-1jv, PR #64), 06b.1-C (loreweaver-q0d, PR #65). The campaign bible is now a trustworthy always-on safety net: priorBible is fed back into every extraction with a no-omit instruction (5l8), the CLI rollup wires it through (1jv), and a gated live-API test (q0d) proves the model honors the instruction across 10 iterations. Closed-threads ledger and per-arc bibles remain deferred non-goals.
